segments.content:
Chapter 6: Childhood Friend Finally Wised Up? What's It Like to Have a Photographic Memory?

As requested: it's awesome.

I could memorize English vocabulary with a single glance, and my mind had never been so clear.

But there was no need to memorize English slang, like "four generations under one roof" as "family 4.0," "hot spring" as "gulugulu water," or "third concubine" as "three bitches."

Simple and easy. A piece of cake.

Jiang Nian was glad he had the habit of lugging home all the important textbooks for every subject during the holidays. Even though he hadn't flipped a single page, it still gave him the feeling of having secretly put in the effort.

Now, they came in handy. It was awesome, simply wonderful.

For the entire afternoon, Jiang Nian was immersed in the ocean of learning. Those tiny bits of knowledge were like massive swarms of krill, swallowed whole by a whale.

Next door, Xu Qianqian groggily awoke from her afternoon nap, gritting her silvery teeth.

"So noisy!"

No matter how she covered her ears, Jiang Nian's excited sighs and groans still managed to find their way in. He'd been at it for half the day; she had no idea what he was so worked up about.

Could it be the legendary, uh... "male Daoist ritual"?

As the daughter of an andrologist, Xu Qianqian wasn't lacking in common sense. She just thought Jiang Nian was being a bit deranged. If you're going to watch a movie, can you not be so loud and take so long?

And in broad daylight, too. I even have my lights off!

Jiang Nian had been so absorbed in his morning studies that he passed out, feeling like his pig brain was a bit overloaded. He slept all the way until the afternoon, only waking up when he faintly heard a knock on the door.

"Hello, delivery!"

He remembered taking a call from the courier that morning. He pulled open the door. The delivery man tipped the brim of his cap, a small cart in hand. He sized Jiang Nian up, seeming a little surprised.

"Mr. Jiang?"

"Yes."

After signing for it, Jiang Nian tried on his shoes. The soles of the sneakers were very soft. Two hundred yuan a pair; a thousand yuan had gotten new shoes for the whole family. It was a pretty good deal.

He was hungry and not in the mood to keep looking at the shoes. He slipped on a pair and went downstairs to eat.

In the past, if he had bought new shoes, he would have endured his hunger to jump around in them for a minute or two. But now, he had a cold, hard two thousand yuan sitting in his bank account.

With a huge sum of two thousand yuan, why would he jump around like a jackass?

In the evening, Jiang Nian was still sleepy, but he had to get ready for evening self-study at school.

Perhaps it was because of the breakfast he had delivered, or for some other reason, but Xu Qianqian, for the first time ever, hadn't left ahead of him. Instead, she was sitting in his living room, waiting.

The last time she'd done that was back in middle school.

Jiang Nian was somewhat overwhelmed by the unexpected favor.

"Why are you willing to wait for me?"

Hearing this, Xu Qianqian stood up as if to leave.

"Hmph."

"Hey, hey, milady, please wait. Pretend I didn't say anything." Jiang Nian was packing his school bag and quickly reached out to stop her. "Please sit, please sit. Give me two minutes."

Xu Qianqian glanced down at his paw, said nothing, and sat back down on the sofa. Her eyes lifted to watch Jiang Nian toss his English vocabulary booklet to the side, and she couldn't help but speak up.

"Jiang Nian, what did you say to me this morning?"

"What do you mean?"

"You're not even bringing your vocabulary booklet! You said this morning you were going to memorize vocabulary, and this afternoon you're just tossing the booklet aside?" Xu Qianqian was a bit speechless, shooting him a glance.

"The Gaokao only looks at your total score. Your English is so bad, if you improved it by even a few dozen points, you could get into a decent—"

She didn't finish her sentence. Xu Qianqian realized that with Jiang Nian's abysmal grades that would make his parents despair, an improvement of a few dozen points in English would get him into a decent vocational college.

"Aiya, it's hard to explain to you right now." Jiang Nian then tossed out his Chinese, Biology, Chemistry, and Physics booklets, making Xu Qianqian's eyes go wide.

"Are you trying to die, Jiang Nian? I'm going to tell Auntie Li!" It was an evening in September. Dusk and the molten gold of the sunset blended together, and the streetlights were bright.

On the old streets of the small county town were five or six-story self-built houses, with a crisscrossing web of electrical wires. The alleys were narrow and dim. The only advantage was that the buildings didn't block the light, so there was good sun exposure.

Xu Qianqian and Jiang Nian emerged from a dim alley. Zhennan County Middle School was not far away. The area where both their families lived was similar to a shantytown.

The two of them rarely walked together like this, and the atmosphere was a little strange.

As they neared the school gate, Xu Qianqian, who was half a step behind Jiang Nian, clutched her backpack strap. She frowned and hesitated for a moment before speaking.

"You should interact less with Zhou Yuting's group in the future. They're not good people."

Jiang Nian couldn't agree more.

Ever since Zhou Yuting's birthday party, he had seen their true colors. They treated him like a complete clown, constantly putting him down to prop up Liu Feipeng.

There was no particular reason for it, other than Liu Feipeng wanting to pursue Zhou Yuting. If you can't elevate yourself, then put others down, using the comparison to highlight your own maturity.

Among them, Jiang Nian had no money and poor grades. All he had was his physique and looks, which made him an even bigger target for public criticism.

Xu Qianqian was only saying this because of yesterday's steamed chicken in lotus leaf and the breakfast. Although she and Jiang Nian didn't get along, she had a soft spot after being fed. After all, they were playmates who had grown up together.

Even though this "toxic childhood friend" of hers was a bit dim-witted, his heart wasn't bad, and his cooking was quite good. No matter what, it wasn't up to others to bully him.

In her eyes, Zhou Yuting was a green tea bitch, a total tramp. Only a straight-laced guy like Jiang Nian would be played like a fiddle and led around by the nose by her.

She had said similar things before, but Jiang Nian had always shot her down. Today, she was just saying it one last time. She wouldn't bring it up again.

But to her surprise, Jiang Nian turned around, his black hair framing his bright eyes, and nodded seriously.

"Mm, I know."

He knows?

Xu Qianqian was a bit stunned. When did he wise up?

She was still in a daze from the shock well into the first session of evening self-study after getting to the classroom. Had the Jiang family's ancestral graves started smoking? Had the simp seen the light?

In the brightly lit classroom, the only sound was the rustling of pages turning and homework being done.

"Qianqian, what's wrong with you?" Her deskmate Yang Man poked Xu Qianqian's fair arm, which was cool and soft. "You've been spacing out for almost the whole period. Did something happen?"

"Huh?" Xu Qianqian snapped back to reality. "No, it's nothing."

She shook her head, thinking to herself, *What on earth am I doing, wasting an entire evening self-study session over Jiang Nian!* She took a deep breath and lowered her head to work on practice problems.

Jiang Nian was in the class next door. The two classes were adjacent, but worlds apart in level.

The students at Zhennan County Middle School were divided into four tiers: Key (Key Support), Parallel (Regular), Olympiad, and Zero Class, in ascending order.

The Key classes were all arranged on the first and second floors, close to the dean's office on the first floor, making them easier to manage if they got noisy. The Olympiad and Zero classes were mostly on the third and fourth floors, the pride of the heavens.

The Parallel classes had it rough; all the workhorses were thrown onto the fifth and sixth floors.

Xu Qianqian's class was an Olympiad Science class. Jiang Nian's was a Parallel Science class. He was considered extremely lucky to have been assigned to the fourth floor, very close to Xu Qianqian's class.

Their head teacher said it was so they could "absorb the spiritual energy." Jiang Nian begged to differ.

For convenience, both classes had almost all the same subject teachers. With the same test papers, the Olympiad class would get the lecture first before the teacher went back to the Parallel class to teach it. What chance did they have?

The evening self-study session was silent. Jiang Nian buried his head in his practice problems.

The reward from the system was so useful. After an afternoon of memorizing, he had completely committed the thirty-five hundred Gaokao vocabulary words to memory. Tackling the English practice papers was basically no trouble at all.

(End of this chapter)
